idea-plugin.name: Jolta: Java Version Manager
idea-plugin.description:
The JDK your project asks for, selected for you — in the IDE, the terminal, and CI.

Pin a Java version once with a .java-version file and jolta keeps everything on it. This plugin makes IntelliJ IDEA one of the things that agrees.

  • Nothing to configure. Open a pinned project and the Project SDK, the Gradle JVM, and the Maven importer JDK are already right.
  • Set the version from the IDE. Pick a JDK from the status bar or Tools → Jolta and the pin is written for you — so your teammates, your terminal, and CI land on the same JDK. Don't have it? It downloads.
  • Live. Run jolta pin 25 in any terminal, or pull a teammate's commit, and the IDE follows within seconds. No restart, no re-import.
  • Run configurations too. JAVA_HOME and PATH point at the pinned JDK, so anything your tests shell out to agrees with the IDE.
  • SDK entries that don't rot. jolta upgrade moves a JDK and the SDK entry is repointed — never left dangling for you to clean up by hand.
  • It stays out of unpinned projects. No pin and no jolta default means the plugin leaves your SDK exactly as you set it.

Requires the jolta CLI: brew install OneAppPlatform/tap/jolta (or see the install guide). On macOS and Linux the plugin offers to install it for you.

Windows: the CLI needs a manual install for now — download jolta-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from the releases page, unzip it, and run .\jolta.exe setup. Setup is first-class on Windows: it adds the shims to your user PATH in the registry and installs the JAVA_HOME hook for PowerShell. Sorry for the extra step — a winget package is submitted and awaiting review, which will make this a one-liner.

Support: free and open source (MIT). Questions, bugs and feature requests go to the issue tracker — that's the fastest way to reach us, and it means the answer helps the next person too.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

First release.

  • Opens a pinned project with the Project SDK, Gradle JVM and Maven importer JDK already set — nothing to configure.
  • Set the Java version from the IDE: pick a JDK from the status bar or Tools → Jolta and the .java-version pin is written for you. A version you don't have yet is downloaded.
  • Live: jolta pin 25 in any terminal, or a teammate's commit, and the IDE follows within seconds.
  • JAVA_HOME and PATH point at the pin for Java run configurations, so anything they shell out to agrees with the IDE.
  • SDK entries are repointed after jolta upgrade instead of being left dangling.
  • Offers to pin an unpinned project to the JDK it is already using, and leaves projects jolta doesn't govern completely alone.
  • Reports genuinely broken configuration — a JDK that has gone from disk, or a .java-version and .sdkmanrc that disagree — and stays quiet about differences that are deliberate, such as a Gradle toolchain.
  • Offers to install the jolta CLI if it isn't there.
